backlog.title: Why Testing Automated Driving Is Harder Than It Looks
backlog.summary:
Instead of waiting for rare situations to occur on public roads, engineers can create those situations virtually. 
The post Why Testing Automated Driving Is Harder Than It Looks appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The 'scenario explosion' problem makes physical road testing insufficient for validating ADAS, as the number of variables in weather, traffic, and sensor conditions is effectively infinite.
Validation is evolving into a portfolio management challenge where engineers must use virtual simulation to prove consistent system reliability across millions of potential edge cases.
Proving safety in software-defined vehicles requires rigorous coverage metrics that go far beyond successful navigation of a single urban environment.

backlog.title: Adding Network Security To AI, HPC, And Data Centers
backlog.summary:
The location of security functions such as MACsec or IPsec has become a key architectural decision.
The post Adding Network Security To AI, HPC, And Data Centers appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Modern AI and HPC data centers are shifting toward multi-terabit network speeds, necessitating hardware-accelerated security architectures like MACsec and IPsec.

Architectural decisions regarding security placement—whether in switch ASICs, external PHYs, or pluggable modules—are increasingly driven by total cost of ownership and supply-chain constraints rather than just technical performance.

Transport-level security, such as RoCEv2 or Ultra Ethernet, is becoming essential for end-to-end workload protection, requiring security mechanisms that remain transparent to the underlying high-speed fabric.

backlog.title: A new bill could change how the US builds energy infrastructure
backlog.summary: A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US. With the dust barely settled on this week’s momentous midterms, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9. It’s a plan that could finally…
bullets: The Senate is scheduled to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9, a 417-page bill aimed at streamlining the complex federal permitting process for energy infrastructure.
The legislation is technology-neutral, potentially accelerating the deployment of both fossil fuel and renewable energy projects by narrowing permit requirements and imposing strict review deadlines.
The White House and various clean energy industry groups support the bill, with projections suggesting it could unlock 350 gigawatts of new clean energy capacity for the national grid.

The bill faces opposition from environmental groups concerned that the reduction in regulatory oversight could lead to increased industrial pollution and weakened protections under the National Environmental Policy Act.

backlog.title: An Interview With Intuit CEO Sasan Goodarzi About Accounting and AI
backlog.summary: An interview with Intuit CEO Sasan Goodarzi about the working for one of tech's oldest software companies, and how Intuit is leaning into the AI paradigm shift.
bullets: Intuit CEO Sasan Goodarzi outlines the company's strategy to navigate the AI paradigm shift while maintaining its 44-year legacy of software innovation.
The company is actively re-positioning accountants from being primary distribution partners to becoming core customers through the integration of AI-driven tools.
Goodarzi defends Intuit's market position against potential disruption, arguing that strategic acquisitions like Credit Karma and Mailchimp provide a robust platform for future growth.
The interview highlights the evolution of Intuit’s business model, specifically focusing on the transition from legacy products like Quicken to modern, AI-integrated ecosystems.

backlog.title: Memory In Physical AI
backlog.summary:
LPDDR6 becomes an essential ingredient as intelligence moves into autonomous and mobile edge systems.
The post Memory In Physical AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: LPDDR6 memory is emerging as a critical component for autonomous and mobile edge systems, where battery life is the primary constraint on operational utility.
Physical AI applications, such as humanoid robots and drones, require optimized data hierarchies to balance processing efficiency with power consumption.
Industry experts emphasize that extending the runtime of mobile AI platforms necessitates denser, faster memory architectures and more efficient data movement between processors.
The integration of advanced memory technologies is essential to maximize performance in edge-based AI while maintaining cost-effective hardware designs.

backlog.title: The climate case for AI has not been made
backlog.summary: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action. But so far, industries around the world…
bullets: While AI companies project significant emissions reductions by 2035, current market data shows little evidence that major industrial players are adopting the necessary AI-driven strategies.
Academic models suggest AI could cut global emissions by up to 5.4 billion tons annually, but these projections remain largely aspirational rather than operational.
The power sector represents the most concrete potential for AI-driven climate impact through supply and demand forecasting, yet actual deployment remains behind theoretical expectations.

backlog.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
backlog.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where…
bullets: The growing public backlash against data centers is increasingly driven by physical electricity constraints rather than abstract cultural concerns.
Data centers in hubs like Loudoun County, Virginia, now average 54 megawatts of power capacity, exceeding the energy draw of major international airports.
The industry faces a structural challenge where reliance on the existing power grid creates direct competition with local communities for energy resources.

backlog.title: Learning the Language of the Brain’s Cell Types
backlog.summary: How linking neural activity to cell identity will help build models of the brain and reveal new therapeutic targets
bullets: Artificial neural networks rely on uniform computational units, whereas biological brains utilize a diverse array of specialized cell types evolved over millions of years.
The current inability to link specific neuron identities to real-time electrical activity in living brains hinders our understanding of complex cognitive functions and disease pathology.
Researchers propose creating an 'ImageNet for cell types' to standardize a reference dataset that maps specific neuron types to their unique electrical signatures.

Developing this classification system could enable AI to interpret neural recordings from living humans, potentially accelerating the development of biologically realistic AI models and new therapeutic interventions.

backlog.title: Overcoming Silicon Photonics Process Control Challenges in the AI Era
backlog.summary:
How connected inspection, metrology and software can help manufacturers move SiPh and CPO toward high-volume production.
The post Overcoming Silicon Photonics Process Control Challenges in the AI Era appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Silicon photonics (SiPh) and co-packaged optics (CPO) are emerging as essential solutions to overcome the power, heat, and latency bottlenecks of traditional copper interconnects.
Optical performance is highly sensitive to small process variations, requiring significantly tighter control over geometry, films, and material defects than standard semiconductor manufacturing.
Manufacturers must implement connected inspection and metrology software to maintain yield as they transition SiPh and CPO technologies from research to high-volume production.

backlog.title: Shrinking Hybrid Bonding Pitches Push Inspection Limits
backlog.summary:
Existing inspection tools struggle to capture defects, especially those hidden at the bond interface.
The post Shrinking Hybrid Bonding Pitches Push Inspection Limits appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Hybrid bonding is scaling below 10 µm pitches, creating a critical need for inspection tools capable of detecting defects as small as 50 nm at the bond interface.
Particles and surface contamination are primary failure drivers, as even nanoscale debris can cause delamination or bonding voids that result in catastrophic yield loss.
Conventional metrology is struggling to differentiate killer defects from minor topographical variations, forcing reliance on advanced optical, IR, and X-ray inspection methods.

backlog.title: Which Passing Chips Need More Testing?
backlog.summary:
Manufacturers are using test data and predictive models to identify marginal chips and determine when additional screening is justified.
The post Which Passing Chips Need More Testing? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Standard wafer sort and final tests often fail to identify marginal chips that pass electrical checks but are prone to field failures due to timing margins or subtle reliability weaknesses.
Manufacturers are increasingly using predictive models and internal parametric measurements to identify statistical outliers among passing parts, avoiding the high cost of universal retesting.
The industry faces a difficult trade-off between the high cost of additional test patterns and the extreme expense of field failures in advanced, high-value AI silicon.

backlog.title: Reducing Lithography Learning Cycles To Accelerate FOPLP Ramps
backlog.summary:
How yield prediction technology can reduce trial-and-error in advanced packaging lithography.
The post Reducing Lithography Learning Cycles To Accelerate FOPLP Ramps appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) offers superior substrate utilization compared to traditional wafers, with 510x515mm panels achieving up to 74% utilization versus 55% for 300mm wafers.
Scaling to larger panels introduces non-uniform pattern distortion and die shift, making traditional global correction strategies insufficient for high-yield production.
Manufacturers must balance yield and throughput by choosing between zone, die-by-die, or site-by-site correction, as each method imposes different penalties on production speed.

backlog.title: Why Integrated Gate Drive Regulation Matters For High Reliability Space GaN Designs
backlog.summary:
Eliminating the need for a separate bias regulator dedicated to the gate driver for a more streamlined power architecture.
The post Why Integrated Gate Drive Regulation Matters For High Reliability Space GaN Designs appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Integrating low dropout regulators (LDOs) directly into GaN gate drivers simplifies power architectures for space applications by eliminating the need for external bias circuits.
Precise voltage regulation is critical for GaN devices, as even minor fluctuations can degrade switching efficiency, increase EMI, and compromise long-term reliability in extreme environments.
Reducing the total bill of materials (BOM) through integration lowers weight and qualification costs, which are significant barriers for satellite and aerospace power system designs.

backlog.title: Fitting AI Models To Edge Applications
backlog.summary:
Compression can shrink AI models, but efficient edge deployment starts with matching the architecture to the workload and hardware limits.
The post Fitting AI Models To Edge Applications appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Edge AI deployment is shifting focus from raw compute power to bandwidth and memory efficiency, as high-parameter models often exceed the power and thermal limits of embedded devices.
Techniques such as quantization, self-compression, and distillation are critical for right-sizing models to match specific hardware constraints without sacrificing intelligence.
Designers must define the application's purpose first to avoid the performance penalties associated with oversized models in constrained environments like IoT and automotive systems.

backlog.title: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
backlog.summary: As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed…
bullets: Specialty chemical manufacturer Lubrizol is utilizing AI and cloud-based digital modeling to accelerate R&D cycles and evaluate sustainable material formulations.
The company employs 'fusion teams' to bridge the gap between data scientists and traditional chemists, ensuring that AI tools augment rather than replace scientific judgment.
Cloud infrastructure allows chemical firms to scale research capabilities without the capital expenditure required to build and maintain proprietary data centers.

backlog.title: Streaming Scan Network Test Over PCIe
backlog.summary:
Changing test strategies put a premium on how closely the design ecosystem and the test ecosystem line up. 
The post Streaming Scan Network Test Over PCIe appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Siemens’ Streaming Scan Network (SSN) and In-System Test allow test data to be delivered via functional interfaces like PCIe, eliminating the need for dedicated test ports.
This approach enables the use of standard AXI buses to packetize and share scan data across multiple cores, significantly improving test efficiency for complex chiplet-based designs.

Integration with Teradyne’s UltraFLEXplus allows engineers to maintain a unified programming model from initial bring-up through high-volume production, reducing the gap between design and test teams.

backlog.title: Evolving metal extraction processes
backlog.summary: The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible. Yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems…
bullets: The metals industry is facing a strategic inflection point where traditional extraction methods are being challenged by the need for lower-carbon production and improved supply chain resilience.

Western economies are increasingly vulnerable due to a decline in domestic processing capacity for critical minerals, which are essential for sectors ranging from aerospace to defense and energy systems.

Outokumpu’s 'EvoMaterials' platform highlights a shift toward reimagining fundamental metallurgical science to address modern constraints, such as the 67% lower carbon footprint achieved in their ferrochrome production.

As demand for specialty metals like chromium rises, the industry is moving toward a model where geographic origin and carbon footprint are as critical to supply chain strategy as cost and availability.

backlog.title: College Grads And AI
backlog.summary:
Computer science majors may be in an awkward space; EE grads are fine for now.
The post College Grads And AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The adoption of AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot and Cursor is leading to a hiring slowdown for entry-level computer science roles as developer productivity increases.
While software-focused roles face uncertainty, demand for specialized chip design expertise remains more stable because these roles require deep domain knowledge beyond standard programming.
Data science graduates appear to be experiencing more significant employment disruption from AI automation compared to traditional computer science and electrical engineering graduates.

backlog.title: Turning Conv2D Into A Practical GPU Compute Pattern
backlog.summary:
A reusable optimization mindset for engineers building GPU compute kernels.
The post Turning Conv2D Into A Practical GPU Compute Pattern appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Engineers can optimize 2D convolution performance by reframing it as a structured matrix multiplication problem rather than a unique mathematical primitive.
Using NHWC data layouts allows spatial feature vectors to be processed as matrix rows, significantly simplifying implementation and improving cache efficiency on GPU hardware.
This approach reduces the complexity of custom kernel development by leveraging well-understood loop ordering and memory traffic management strategies.

backlog.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.

backlog.title: The Definitive AFM Modes Handbook: 2026 Edition

A comprehensive guide to expanding materials research capabilities.

bullets: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) has evolved from basic topographical mapping to a critical analytical tool for characterizing soft, fragile materials at the atomic scale.

backlog.title: Hardware-Based Location Checks Target AI Chip Smuggling (Texas A&M)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at Texas A&M University published “5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices.” Abstract: “Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip’s distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its... » read more
The post Hardware-Based Location Checks Target AI Chip Smuggling (Texas A&M) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at Texas A&M developed '5G CATS,' a hardware-based location verification system designed to enforce export controls on high-end AI accelerators.
The system integrates a 5G radio directly into the GPU package, bypassing host software and baseboard management controllers to prevent tampering.
Simulations show the system can detect fiber-based traffic relay attacks from 300 km away, significantly outperforming existing power-line or software-based verification methods.
By using 5G URLLC base stations and short-lived execution leases, the technology provides a robust mechanism to ensure AI chips remain within authorized geographic regions.

backlog.title: Single-Crystal High-κ Dielectric Enables Low-Power 2D CFETs (NUS et al.)
backlog.summary:
Researchers led by the National University of Singapore  and Nexstrom published “Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics.” Abstract Excerpt: “Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal... » read more
The post Single-Crystal High-κ Dielectric Enables Low-Power 2D CFETs (NUS et al.) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from NUS and Nexstrom demonstrated wafer-scale, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectrics integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides.
This integration enables complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) to achieve subthreshold swings near the thermal limit and record-low hysteresis.

The resulting inverters demonstrate high voltage gain and large noise margins while maintaining subpicowatt static power consumption, marking a significant step for ultra-low-power 2D semiconductor applications.

backlog.title: What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
backlog.summary: It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks, taking place this time in Antalya, Turkey. COP31 officially kicked off on November 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world. Turkey and Australia are cohosting this…
bullets: COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, is currently focused on the critical tension between fossil fuel reduction and the mobilization of climate finance.
The US is absent from formal negotiations for the second consecutive year following its withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and the UN Framework Committee on Climate Change.
Global warming is projected to exceed the 1.5 °C threshold within the next few years, rendering the original Paris Agreement goals increasingly difficult to achieve.
Financial targets remain a major hurdle, with a goal of $300 billion annually by 2035, despite rich nations providing only $136.7 billion in 2024.

backlog.title: UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs
backlog.summary:
The differences and engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.
The post UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys highlights that implementing UCIe standards requires distinct engineering strategies depending on whether the design uses 2.5D or 3D packaging.

In 2.5D designs, engineers must manage insertion loss and crosstalk across package channels, whereas 3D designs leverage high-density vertical connections to reduce the need for high-speed serialization.
The white paper emphasizes that 3D integration fundamentally alters reliability, testing, and interface design, necessitating a shift in how UCIe IP is aligned with package topology.

backlog.title: Embedded ECC Protects AI Weights Against Bit-Flip Attacks (University of Florida)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at the University of Florida published “SANAI: Secure ECC Distributed Keyed Parity Embedded in Weights for Protecting Neural Networks against Bit-Flip Attacks.” Abstract Excerpt: “We propose SANAI, a sensitivity-guided, bit-plane-selective scheme that protects critical model weights against bit flips with zero additional parity-storage overhead. SANAI secures parity through keyed embedding across a two-dimensional weight... » read more
The post Embedded ECC Protects AI Weights Against Bit-Flip Attacks (University of Florida) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The University of Florida introduced 'SANAI,' a security scheme that embeds error-correcting code (ECC) directly into neural network weights to defend against bit-flip attacks.
The method utilizes sensitivity-guided, bit-plane-selective protection, allowing for security implementation with zero additional parity-storage overhead.
By employing spread-transform dither modulation and keyed interleaving, the system binds parity to a secret key and disperses concentrated attacks across codewords to maintain model integrity.

backlog.title: Variable-Length Prompts on Chimera GPNPU
backlog.summary:
How a flexible binary can serve every length up to the capacity you set.
The post Variable-Length Prompts on Chimera GPNPU appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Quadric's Chimera GPNPU architecture addresses the inefficiency of padding in AI inference by allowing a single compiled binary to handle variable-length prompts.
Traditional inference stacks often require building separate binaries for different prompt lengths, leading to wasted compute cycles on padding for shorter inputs.

The GPNPU approach optimizes resource utilization by dynamically adapting to prompt length, which is critical for edge devices that must handle diverse workloads ranging from short commands to long documents.

backlog.title: Optimized E-Beam Evaporation Reduces Metal-Semiconductor Contact Degradation (RWTH Aachen)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at RWTH Aachen University published “Mitigating the degradation of metal–semiconductor contacts with optimized electron beam evaporation.” Abstract “An optimized electron beam evaporation (EBE) setup is presented that allows the suppression of charged particle bombardment of 4” semiconductor samples during metal coating. In-situ measurements of charge carrier flux for different tool configurations are carried out.... » read more
The post Optimized E-Beam Evaporation Reduces Metal-Semiconductor Contact Degradation (RWTH Aachen) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: RWTH Aachen researchers developed an optimized electron beam evaporation (EBE) setup that suppresses charged particle bombardment during metal coating.
The technique reduces Fermi level pinning in metal-semiconductor contacts, leading to higher Schottky barriers in n-type silicon.
This process improvement offers a more reliable fabrication method for high-performance Schottky diodes by mitigating contact degradation during the deposition phase.
